subject: End markers
notes: cite.py: OK §10.7.4 '1) An end marker indicates the end of the specified source unit.' The grammar closes a unit at its end marker: nestedProgram requires endProgramHeader, and classDefinition, factory, object, method and interface each end in their own END. p4 shows a unit contained in another and closed by END PROGRAM running as the nested program. In a program that breaks SR3 (p3), the marker closes the innermost open unit whatever name it gives. That is the SR3 under-reject and does not change what a conforming program means. No spec-derived test covers this directly. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 1985+ (program); 2002+ (OO/function units)
